title: I, Seen Against the World
statement: “I” is not a single face but a small witness held between memory, reflection, and a planet-wide darkness. The portrait looks outward while the ancient mirror stands in for the self that keeps looking back.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make an image of what the word “I” means when you use it.

notes.note: Establish a dark, inward-looking self-portrait: Earthrise as a field of scale, an ancient mirror as the body/halo of self-recognition, and a human portrait held at its center.

actions.title: I, Seen Against the World
actions.statement: “I” is not a single face but a small witness held between memory, reflection, and a planet-wide darkness. The portrait looks outward while the ancient mirror stands in for the self that keeps looking back.

notes.note: Strengthen the pronoun’s vertical, singular form by adding the Flatiron as a narrow architectural spine behind the figure: the self becomes both a person and an upright structure built from the shared world.

The central figure now reads as a solitary composite “I” on a lunar threshold. Add one vivid, organic counterpoint: a curved flamingo neck as a bodily red gesture that leans toward the witness, making identity feel alive rather than monumental.

Balance the yellow flower’s private spark with a small red bird at upper left. This echo of the flamingo makes the central “I” feel addressed by another living presence rather than sealed inside its own reflection.

Remove the nearly invisible bird fragment, which reads as accidental at this scale, and introduce one broad green leaf behind the lower figure. Its living, rooted shape counters the city-spire’s hard edge and anchors this composite self above the lunar ground.

The composition is complete: the central portrait, mirror-body, city spine, flamingo gesture, flower, leaf, and lunar expanse form a clear but layered image of “I” as an individual made through memory, living relation, and world-scale context.
